cohort: The study included 13,988 infants born before 29 weeks' gestation and admitted to a level 3 neonatal intensive care unit in Canada between 2009 and 2018, who underwent neurodevelopmental assessments at 18-24 months corrected age.
finding: Infants born before 29 weeks' gestation and exposed to maternal diabetes in utero had increased odds of neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI), language delays, and motor delays, but no significant difference was found in significant NDI (sNDI) compared to unexposed infants.
